input: Make a homemade holiday wreath from foraged branches

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The type of holiday (Christmas, winter solstice, general winter) shapes the aesthetic, color palette, and symbolic elements to include — e.g., a Christmas wreath leans into red and green, while a solstice wreath might use more neutral, earthy tones.
Knowing whether this is a solo project or involves others (e.g., kids, a group craft session) changes the complexity of techniques, safety considerations, and how the steps should be broken down.
Where the wreath will be displayed (indoor vs. outdoor, front door vs. mantel) affects the size, durability requirements, and what materials will hold up well.

Knowing what foraged materials are actually available in the user's local environment (e.g., pine, cedar, eucalyptus, holly, bare twigs) is the single biggest constraint — the plan must be built around what exists nearby.
Whether the user has a wreath form, wire, floral tape, or other basic supplies on hand determines whether the plan needs to include a materials-sourcing step or can go straight to construction.
The desired style (lush and full, minimalist and modern, rustic/naturalistic, maximalist with ribbons and ornaments) fundamentally changes which materials to gather and how to arrange them.

Understanding the user's experience level with crafting or wreath-making determines how detailed the instructions need to be — a beginner needs step-by-step guidance, while an experienced crafter may just need inspiration and a materials list.

gold.taskTitle: Make a homemade holiday wreath from foraged branches
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to create a handmade holiday wreath using branches and materials gathered from nature.

questions.title: Which holiday or season is this wreath celebrating?
questions.description: Identify the specific holiday or theme (Christmas, Hanukkah, winter solstice, general winter/New Year) to align color palette, symbols, and materials.

questions.title: Where exactly will the finished wreath be displayed?
questions.description: Determine the intended display location (front door, interior wall, mantel, table centerpiece) to guide size, durability, and construction choices.

questions.title: What forageable plants or branches grow near you?
questions.description: Identify locally available natural materials (e.g., pine, cedar, holly, eucalyptus, bare oak twigs, rosehips) since the entire plan depends on what the user can actually gather.

questions.title: Do you already have a wreath form or basic craft supplies?
questions.description: Find out whether the user has a wire or grapevine wreath form, floral wire, clippers, or hot glue gun — or if acquiring supplies needs to be part of the plan.

questions.title: What visual style are you going for with this wreath?
questions.description: Clarify the aesthetic direction — rustic and naturalistic, lush and traditional, minimalist and modern, or maximalist with ribbons and ornaments — to shape material selection and arrangement.

questions.title: Will you be making this alone or with others?
questions.description: Determine if this is a solo project or a group/family activity (including children) to adjust technique complexity, safety notes, and step pacing.

questions.title: How much crafting or wreath-making experience do you have?
questions.description: Gauge the user's skill level to calibrate how detailed the instructions should be — from full beginner step-by-step guidance to a higher-level materials and structure outline.
